note: 'Hurry,” said the king to Haman, “and do just as you proposed. Take the robe and the horse to Mordecai the Jew' (Esth 6:10) -- the charge Haman had framed for himself.

'if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request' (Esth 5:8); 'grant me my life as my petition, and the lives of my people as my request' (Esth 7:3); and again 'weeping and begged him to revoke the evil scheme of Haman' (Esth 8:3).

'Then Esther summoned Hathach ... and she dispatched him to Mordecai to learn what was troubling him and why' (Esth 4:5); 'Then Esther spoke to Hathach and instructed him to tell Mordecai,' (Esth 4:10).
'Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day' (Esth 4:16).
held: inside quoted speech (the Berean's quotation marks), speaker not on record

note: The charge runs both ways by the end of the chapter: 'So Mordecai went and did all that Esther had instructed him.' (Esth 4:17). She began the book under his charge and ends it giving her own.

He carried the charge rather than laying one: 'So Hathach went out to Mordecai' (Esth 4:6), and 'Hathach went back and relayed Mordecai's response to Esther' (Esth 4:9). Recorded so the chain between the palace and the gate is visible; the words are Esther's and Mordecai's, not his.

Twice, and the second reverses the first. 'Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.' (Esth 2:10, repeated 2:20); then 'urging her to approach the king, implore his favor, and plead before him for her people' (Esth 4:8).
